label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
★★★★☆

Moved from Phibsborough to Drumcondra on Saturday 17th October with Kilbarrack Van Co. Two bed flat, but honestly mostly my own stuff, so not a massive job. The catch was the new place is a 4th floor walk-up with no lift, which is the bit I was dreading. Writing this up properly because I read loads of reviews before booking and the useful ones were the ones that actually said what happened.

**Booking and price**
Booked through their website, €50 deposit by Revolut, no hassle. The quote was €340 for up to 4 hours with two lads and the van. Every other quote I got was €450 or more for the same thing, so on price alone they were miles ahead. The whole job took about three and a half hours, so we came in under the time.

**The not so good bit, the lateness**
They were meant to arrive at 9 and turned up at half 10. To be fair I got a text at 8:40 saying the job before had overrun, so I wasn't left wondering if they were coming at all. Still, I spent the guts of an hour and a half sitting on boxes with a cold coffee. For me it wasn't the end of the world because I had nothing else on that day. But if you're on a tight handover with a landlord, or you have to be out of your old place by a set time, I'd be upfront about that when you book. Maybe ask for the first slot of the day so there's no job before yours to run over.

Dessie knocked €40 off the bill afterwards because of the delay. I didn't ask him to, he just did it, which I thought was decent of him and says a lot about how he runs things.

**The lads on the day**
Once they got going they were sound and quick. The couch wouldn't go round the turn on the 3rd floor stairs. I was already picturing it living on the landing forever, but the younger lad (Kev, I think?) pulled an allen key out of his pocket, took the legs off, and it went straight in. Two minutes, no drama. They also put my bed back together without me asking, and took away a flat pack shelf I didn't want anymore, which saved me a trip.

**The other not so good bit, the lamp**
Everything was wrapped in blankets except my brass floor lamp, and the base got chipped. It was my nanny's lamp so I was a bit gutted, but I'm not making a huge thing of it. It's the kind of thing that's easy to miss on a busy day, but it's worth saying. So lads, wrap the lamps! And for anyone moving: if you've something that matters to you, point it out to them at the start, or wrap it yourself before they arrive. I wish I had.

**Would I use them again?**
Yeah, I would. Best value I found by a long way, the lads worked hard, the stairs didn't faze them, and Dessie dealt with the lateness fairly without me having to chase it. Four stars rather than five because of the delay and the lamp, and I think that's fair. If you're flexible on the day and you flag your fragile bits up front, I'd recommend them.

---

The review uses the euro sign and "Kev, I think?" since you weren't sure of his name. If you'd rather not name him at all, swap it for "the younger lad". Should come in around 550 words.
